name: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72
model: Vera Rubin NVL72 (DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 / OEM MGX builds; formerly branded NVL144)
description: 48U NVIDIA MGX (Oberon) rack: 18 x 1U compute trays (each 2 Vera CPUs + 4 Rubin GPUs, 100% liquid-cooled, 8 x 800G OSFP from ConnectX-9 SuperNICs plus a BlueField-4 with 2 x 400G), 9 NVLink 6 switch trays (one 72-GPU domain) and 4 NVLink cable cartridges. Power: 4 x 3U 110 kW power shelves (6 x 18.3 kW air-cooled PSUs each, two 100 A whips per shelf at 415-480 V AC), three needed for full load, feeding a liquid-cooled 54 V DC, 5,000 A busbar; shelves add bulk energy storage for power smoothing (NVIDIA: 20x more than prior generation). 800 V DC: NVIDIA demonstrated an 800 VDC power sidecar feeding an NVL72 rack (July 2026, press), so dc_800v is listed as a supported option; the standard DGX configuration is AC-fed shelves. Rack power is not published by NVIDIA: Max-Q / Max-P provisioning profiles are reported at about 190 / 230 kW.

nominal_power_w.note: press report: supply-chain analysis (Ming-Chi Kuo) of ~190 kW Max-Q and ~230 kW Max-P profiles (GPU ~1.8 / 2.3 kW). NVIDIA publishes no rack power figure. NVIDIA's RA gives ~2 MW TDP per 8-rack SU including network, consistent with this range. A press report (The Register, Aug 2026) quoting 120 kW looks like a GB200-era figure and is not used.

peak_power_w.note: Gigabyte: rack power consumption up to 240 kW. Supermicro sizes its cooling for 227 kW per rack. Shelf capacity is 3 x 110 kW = 330 kW with one redundant shelf.

power_shelves.note: NVIDIA DGX VR user guide: four shelves per rack. The DGX VR SuperPOD RA adds that only three are required for full rack power (one redundant).

shelf_rating_w.note: 3U shelf, 6 x 18.3 kW PSUs, AC input 415-480 V

liquid_fraction.note: NVIDIA: compute trays are 100% liquid-cooled and the busbar is liquid-cooled. The power shelf PSUs are air-cooled (NVIDIA DGX VR guide), so conversion losses (~3-4% of rack power) plus management switches and optics go to air. No vendor split published.

max_coolant_supply_c.note: NVIDIA lists a 45 C inlet temperature; NVIDIA states a heat exchanger (no chiller) can cool the system at or below 45 C inlet.

rack_pressure_drop_kpa.note: not published by NVIDIA or OEMs as of 2026-10

flow_lpm_per_kw.note: required rack flow not published as of 2026-10; GB300 NVL72 needs 0.5-1.5 L/min/kW depending on supply temperature (Lenovo), a likely similar range

thermal.quick_disconnect: not published; rear manifold with blind-mate QDs per NVIDIA MGX reference (GB300 generation used UQDB04)

depth_mm.note: Gigabyte DLB5-CB0: 1,200 mm. The Register (press) gives the NVIDIA MGX rack as ~1,068 mm deep, which matches the GB300 MGX rack without extension frame. Plan for 1,200 mm.

weight_kg.note: press report: The Register (25 Aug 2026) quotes NVIDIA saying each unit plus rack weighs roughly 4,000 lb (~1,800 kg). Plausible versus GB300 NVL72 (~1,360-1,580 kg) given full cold-plate coverage, liquid-cooled 5,000 A busbar and 3U 110 kW shelves. No OEM weight published.

feet.note: MGX rack with casters and four corner leveling feet assumed; no point-load data published

service_clearance_front_mm.note: NVIDIA's MGX rack front service clearance (33 in) from its DGX B300 guide, assumed to apply to the same MGX rack family

service_clearance_rear_mm.note: not published; rear access needed for manifolds, busbar and NVLink cartridges

scale_out_ports.note: 8 x 800G OSFP (ConnectX-9, 1.6 Tb/s per GPU) per tray x 18 trays; NVIDIA RA: two compute-fabric planes, eight Quantum-X800 connections per tray. BlueField-4 2 x 400G per tray not counted.

scale_up_bandwidth_tbps.note: NVIDIA product page: 216 TB/s (3 TB/s per GPU, footnoted 'at-scale AI factory with MaxLPS'); NVIDIA DGX VR SuperPOD RA: 3.6 TB/s per GPU (259 TB/s). 216-259 TB/s = 1,728-2,074 Tb/s.

switch_slots.note: compute rack; two in-rack out-of-band management switches only

network.port_media: OSFP 800G on front of trays (ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, two ports per 1.6T NIC)

fp4_pflops.note: NVFP4 training, dense. NVIDIA's NVFP4 inference headline is 3,600 PFLOPS (sparse).
